research_rationale:
Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002 (67 FR 69985), Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region, issued under sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 1185(a)(1)) and 3 U.S.C. 301, assigns duties for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean region: section 1(a) custody and screening (originally the Attorney General) with a facility possibly at Guantanamo Bay, 1(b) the Secretary of State on persons in need of protection and resettlement, 1(c) the Secretary of Defense on facilities and, in a mass migration, support; section 2 defines mass migration; section 3 contains scope and general provisions. The 14-clause machine inventory covers the whole text from the preamble to section 3(e) and I confirmed it is complete; I corrected it to 13 clauses by merging the 14-character section 3 heading into section 3(a), and the entries 'lead' (the authority recital) and 'sec1' (the lead-in to section 1) are not commands but frame the commands and are carried as operative with the order. The one amending order found is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), section 1, which replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security wherever it appears in section 1; the OFR catalog record for EO 13276 lists no 'Amended by' note and instead reads 'See: EO 12807, May 24, 1992 | Amends: EO 13286, February 28, 2003'; EO 13286 was signed after EO 13276 and its section 1 amends EO 13276, so I read that catalog note as a transposed record of the EO 13286 amendment, not as a second instrument. EO 12807 (Interdiction of Illegal Aliens) is referred to in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) and is not a revocation or amendment of this order. Search of held texts for the number EO 13276 finds the order, EO 13286, the Federal Register copies of those two, 32 CFR 245.9 (which lists EO 13286 as amending EO 13276), two Federal Register copies of Cuba-policy presidential memoranda (the National Security Presidential Memorandum published at 82 FR 48875, October 20, 2017, and the Memorandum of June 30, 2025, 90 FR 38913) that each state they do not affect EO 13276; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches report machine hits (the OFR catalog entries, the text of EO 13286 and the U.S. Code note), none of which revokes, supersedes or ends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The 8 U.S.C. 1182 note prints the order as amended. The order's own text has no end date; the 'until' phrases in section 1(a)(ii) set how long the custody duty lasts for a particular alien, not an end of the clause. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.
